headline: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Carbon and adds /swarm
dek: Google's strongest model leaves restricted testing, per DeepMind.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Carbon leaves testing
body: Google DeepMind rolled out Gemini 4 Carbon to developers, enterprises and consumers, per the company itself.
Before, only a group of cybersecurity specialists had access to the model (Google DeepMind).

points.t: It is in Google AI Studio and Gemini for Business.
Subscribers get it in the Gemini app and AI Mode.
Coordinates a team of agents in Antigravity (The Verge).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Launch price
body: Carbon costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 for output, per DeepMind and Hipertextual.
The Verge estimates that is about a fifth of GPT-6 Astra's price.

stat.cap: per million input tokens, says Hipertextual

items.t: The price doubles in late November (Hipertextual).
DeepMind says it leads CursorBench 4.0 and WANDR.

caption.hook: Google DeepMind rolled out Gemini 4 Carbon to the public and launched the /swarm feature.
body: Per DeepMind, Google's strongest model was limited to cybersecurity specialists and now reaches developers, enterprises and consumers. It is in the Google AI Studio API and Gemini for Business, and Ultra plan subscribers find it in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search and Antigravity.

/swarm, in testing in Antigravity, turns one prompt into a team of agents that check each other in parallel, per The Verge. The launch price is $2 per million input tokens and $10 for output, and it doubles in late November, according to Hipertextual. The Verge estimates Carbon costs about a fifth of GPT-6 Astra.
